speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic X-ray findings indicate no fractures in the pelvic ring or femoral neck; however, alignment is consistent with a posterior dislocation of the right hip. Clinical examination reveals the right leg is shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated with tenderness in the right groin and knee caps. Range of motion is limited in the right leg due to pain and abnormal positioning, while the left leg remains normal. Vital signs show a heart rate of 116 bpm and blood pressure of 132/79 mm Hg.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Hip Dislocation.

The specific positioning of your right leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is the classic presentation for this injury following the rear-end collision. The severe groin pain and knee pain are consistent with the acute trauma and potential associated injuries.
